title: Amnesty International
description: Independent human rights reporting; its Kashmir material is part of any honest reading list.

title: ARChik / The 'Chronicle of the Kings' context
description: Wikipedia's introduction to the Rajatarangini and Kalhana — context for the primary text above.

title: Digital South Asia Library (DSAL)
description: University of Chicago's digitized South Asia collections — dictionaries, gazetteers and journals for the whole region.

title: DSAL Dictionaries collection
description: DSAL's extensive dictionaries of the languages of the north-west — lexical primary sources in searchable form.

title: Falconry in the Valley of the Indus (Burton)
description: Again, because it lives in both shelves: Richard F. Burton's 1852 hawking journal along the Indus — primary color for AJK&K lowlands.

title: Gazetteer of Kashmir and Ladakh
description: A gazetteer of Kashmir and Ladak with routes in the territories — the kind of administrative source you read for its honesty about place.

title: Gazetteer of the World (concise)
description: A careful overview of AJK: status, geography, history and the dispute, with citations chasing onward to primary sources.

title: Government of Azad Jammu & Kashmir
description: The official portal of Azad Jammu and Kashmir — laws, budgets, census and administrative records.

title: HathiTrust
description: A research library partnership digitizing millions of volumes — searchable full text, free to the world.

title: History of Kashmir and the Kashmiris: The Happy Valley
description: W. Wakefield's first-hand account of Kashmir and its people — a direct, plain-spoken primary source.

title: Human Rights Watch
description: Documented reporting on human rights in Kashmir — cite it as a report, not a verdict.

title: Imperial Gazetteer of India (search)
description: Search the 26-volume Imperial Gazetteer from DSAL — the standard turn-of-century reference for every district of the subcontinent.

title: India Office Records
description: The British Library's India Office Records — the central colonial-era documentation of Kashmir and the north-west, described and indexed here.

title: International Crisis Group
description: Field-based conflict analysis; has published Kashmir studies that straddle the two sides.

title: Internet Archive
description: The free digital library behind most of this shelf — and the search engine for more primary sources.

title: Internet Archive advanced search
description: The API/search interface for finding a specific digitized text by title, author or collection.

title: Internet Archive — Kashmir subject
description: The open search for everything labelled Kashmir on the Archive — a fine way to get lost productively.

title: Kalhana's Rajatarangini (trans. M.A. Stein)
description: Stein's standard translation of Kalhana's 12th-century chronicle of the kings of Kashmir — the indispensable primary narrative.

title: Library of Congress — South Asia
description: The Library of Congress, whose South Asia holdings include gazetteers, maps and rare works on Kashmir.

title: Old Maps Online
description: Search and layer historical maps of Kashmir and the north-west across hundreds of collections.

title: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics
description: Official census reports for AJK and other regions — data, not opinion.

title: Panjab Digital Library
description: Thousands of digitized rare books and manuscripts covering Punjab, Kashmir and the north-west.

title: The National Archives (UK)
description: The UK's archives — including the India Office records that hold most colonial-era original documents about Kashmir.

title: The Valley of Kashmir (Lawrence)
description: Walter R. Lawrence's 1895 gazetteer-cum-study of the valley: land, people, agriculture and state under the Maharaja.

title: Travels in Kashmir, Ladak, Iskardo ... and the Countries Adjoining
description: G.T. Vigne's early-19th-century travels across the mountains of the North West — maps and impressions of a Kashmir still medieval.
